chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him):
Regarding the eggs of the sandgrouse (qat), the compensation is one sheep; if the person in ihram consumes it, [the compensation] is like what is in the eggs of the ostrich: one camel.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: the person in ihram (state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.بَكَارَةٌ: a young female animal (used here as a unit of compensation)

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for eating bird eggs while in ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* details the specific *fidya* (compensation) for consuming bird eggs while in *ihram*, establishing a precedent for valuing different species based on their size and rarity. It reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of deriving legal rulings from the Imams' precise measurements, linking the consumption of the sandgrouse to the penalty of a sheep and the ostrich to that of a camel. This ruling underscores the importance of maintaining ritual purity and the economic valuation of natural resources within the framework of Hajj obligations.
